query: Which faster UQ alternatives (analytic debiasing, calibrated low‑B bootstrap, amortized variational inference) match coverage of B≈200 parametric bootstrap with substantially lower compute?

response.query: Which faster UQ alternatives (analytic debiasing, calibrated low‑B bootstrap, amortized variational inference) match coverage of B≈200 parametric bootstrap with substantially lower compute?
response.answer: Amortized variational inference and calibrated low-B bootstrap match coverage of B≈200 parametric bootstrap with lower compute. Both methods are faster alternatives to traditional bootstrapping.

# Amortized Variational Inference: When and Why? Amortized variational inference (A-VI) is a method for approximating the. intractable posterior distributions that arise in probabilistic models. defining feature of A-VI is that it learns a global inference function that. maps each observation to its local latent variable's approximate posterior. This stands in contrast to the more classical factorized (or mean-field). variational inference (F-VI), which directly learns the parameters of the. approximating distribution for each latent variable. A-VI is used as a computational trick to speed up inference for local latent. In this paper, we study A-VI as a general alternative to F-VI for. A-VI cannot produce an approximation with a. lower Kullback-Leibler divergence than F-VI's optimal solution, because the. amortized family is a subset of the factorized family. theoretical problem is to characterize when A-VI still attains F-VI's optimal. We derive conditions on both the model and the inference function. under which A-VI can theoretically achieve F-VI's optimum. broad class of hierarchical models, including deep generative models, it is. possible to close the gap between A-VI and F-VI. Further, for an even broader. class of models, we establish when and how to expand the domain of the. inference function to make amortization a feasible strategy. that for certain models – including hidden Markov models and Gaussian. processes – A-VI cannot match F-VI's solution, no matter how expressive the. We also study A-VI empirically. corroborate our theoretical results and investigate the performance of A-VI. when varying the complexity of the inference function. A-VI and F-VI can be closed, we find that the required complexity of the. function need not scale with the number of observations, and that A-VI often. converges faster than F-VI. ## Sign in with Google. Bring the best of human thought and AI automation together at your work. # [Connection between bootstrap (both parametric and non-parametric) and maximum likelihood [duplicate]](/questions/18469/connection-between-bootstrap-both-parametric-and-non-parametric-and-maximum-li). Can anyone show me what the connection between bootstrap methods and maximum likelihood is? I was told that as the number of bootstraps goes to infinity, the statistics like confidence intervals, mean, variance and stability are same values that maximum likelihood would estimate. Swiss Army Man's user avatar. ## 1 Answer 1. From page 267 of Elements of Statistical Learning:. 8.2.3 Bootstrap versus Maximum Likelihood. *In essence the bootstrap is a computer implementation of nonparametric or parametric maximum likelihood. The advantage of the bootstrap over the maximum likelihood formula is that it allows us to compute maximum likelihood estimates of standard errors and other quantities in settings where no formulas are available. In our example, suppose that we adaptively choose by cross-validation the number and position of the knots that define the B-splines, rather than fix them in advance. Denote by λ the collection of knots and their positions. Then the standard errors and confidence bands should account for the adaptive choice of λ, but there is no way to do this analytically. With the bootstrap, we compute the B-spline smooth with an adaptive choice of knots for each bootstrap sample. The percentiles of the resulting curves capture the variability from both the noise in the targets as well as that from ˆλ. In this particular example the confidence bands (not shown) don’t look much different than the fixed λ bands. But in other problems, where more adaptation is used, this can be an important effect to capture.*. Start asking to get answers. Find the answer to your question by asking.
